cells.tense: You are standing where two people feel with each other rather than about each other, right here, and you are the one holding the pen.
cells.ask: Offer one clear structure here — a plan, a boundary, a way this will work — and watch what it makes room for.
cells.core:
You can carry several things you know about someone at once and still stay in the room with them. You do not flatten a person into one version, and you do not flinch from what you see. People settle around you, because how you take them in is steady and it does not argue. You read the room and you stay connected to it at the same time, and that pair is rarer than either half.

The knowing is not a weight here. It has somewhere to go. Put one clear shape around what you already understand — say how the two of you will handle this — and let that clarity feed what comes next.
cells.sheetLine: You hold what you see about people and stay connected to them anyway.

cells.tense: You are standing where two people feel with each other rather than about each other, braced against a future you are trying to write in advance.
cells.ask: Pick the one direction that is actually yours right now, and let the rest of the possibilities stay unclaimed.
cells.core:
You can read people well and see many things at once, which is why this gets heavy. When several truths land together, the mind races ahead to sort them before anyone has to feel anything. So you pre-solve the other person — what they will need, where this is going, how it ends. The caring is real. It has just moved out in front of the day, into a version of this that has not happened.

That takes you out of the room you are actually in. The way back is not less perception. It is choosing one direction to move toward and letting the rest stay undecided. Radiance comes from what has actually grown, not from what you have already imagined coming true.
cells.sheetLine: You are solving the future of this connection instead of living in it.

cells.tense: You are standing where two people feel with each other rather than about each other, still stopped at a door that is already behind you.
cells.ask: Let one person catch you in something — your instinct, your vision — and give it to them to hold with you.
cells.core:
When it is working, this is the person who knows exactly what someone is going through and says it out loud. You read people, and the reading lands because it comes from somewhere real. People feel less alone near you. They feel understood without having to explain the whole thing, and that is not a small gift to stand next to.

But the offering stopped. What you see is still there; what went quiet is sharing it — letting someone meet you in the knowing rather than watching from just outside. Dreaming comes back after experience has been taken in all the way. Let one person in on what you are seeing, and feel the current move again.

cells.tense: You are standing where two people feel with each other rather than about each other, and your pen is down even though you are still writing.
cells.ask: Catch one moment this week when you already know the fair thing, and say it — even only to yourself.
cells.core:
You feel your way into other people accurately, and that shapes how you treat them every single day. You catch what is happening with someone before anyone names it, and you adjust — you soften, you give room, you say the useful thing at the right moment. That is why people trust what you notice about them. It has been reliable for a long time.

And you describe it as picking up on things, as though the reading were just happening to you. It is not happening to you. There is an honest sense of what is right in you, and it runs in every room you enter. Own one instance of it this week — that is the way back, and it is yours to take.
cells.sheetLine: You already know what is right with people. You keep calling it nothing.
